answer: An agent earns the right to submit a trade by locking a scarce, slashable stake behind its identity. If it uses that identity to double-spend or violate a signed escrow, anyone can present the receipt and trigger a penalty, making it costly to forge a fleet of disposable accounts: each must tie up capital, and each can lose it. Raising one fake agent’s stake raises the cost of the next, so a sybil spiral consumes real resources rather than merely filling an ocean of cheap names.
